subject: Supply runway and graduated autoscale guidance for private GPU farm (StratusAI request)
messages:
From: Morgan SRE <morgan.sre@stratus.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@stratus.ai
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Private deployment capacity ask: Stratus weekly runway targets and burst profile

Vanessa / Jonas,

Thanks for taking this. We're kicking off our private deployment engagement and need a pragmatic sizing recommendation for our on-prem VPC cluster. High-level requirements below — attached is a traffic profile export (stratus_traffic_profile.csv) that shows two weeks of real traffic by token counts per request.

- Sustained target: ~2,500 tokens/sec sustained across 6-hour daytime window (US PST)
- Expected daily peaks: short bursts up to ~20k tokens/sec for ~5-15 minute windows (1-2x per day)
- Model mix: 70% Llama2-13B quantized (fast), 30% custom-finetuned 70B (8-bit) used for long contexts 
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 350ms for generation during sustained periods; we can tolerate up to 600ms p95 during peak bursts if necessary
- Fault tolerance: must maintain degraded service to 60% capacity if any single rack fails
- Network constraints: our site has a 10Gb egress pipe to the cloud for observability and sync; prefer recommendations that minimize egress and NAT hairpinning costs
- Timeline: first production-ready cluster in 6 weeks, with load-testing window in 3 weeks

Ask: Can Redwood propose a runway (initial GPU counts, warm-pool sizing, headroom %, and an autoscale policy with graded fallbacks to smaller quantized variants)? Also need a short list of network guardrails (NAT/egress patterns, MTU changes, and firewall rules) to avoid noisy neighbor issues during peaks.

Goal is to lock the sizing and runway decisions so our procurement team (copied) can start hardware provisioning.

Thanks,
Morgan
Capacity Lead, StratusAI

---
Attachment: stratus_traffic_profile.csv (CSV export, 2 weeks, sample rows included)

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Morgan SRE <morgan.sre@stratus.ai>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment capacity ask: Stratus weekly runway targets and burst profile

Morgan — thanks for the clear profile. We reviewed the CSV and sketched an initial runway workbook (attached: runway_calcs_v2.xlsx). Summary of our recommended assumptions up front so procurement can move: 

1) Baseline sustained cluster (production WARM): aim for 10 x A100-80GB (or equivalent 80GB-class GPUs) dedicated to the L2-13B quantized load. This covers ~2.5k tokens/sec sustained with ~30% headroom for queuing and variance assuming efficient batching/prefix cache.

2) Burst absorption (WARM-POOL + FAST ADMIT): maintain a warm-pool of 6 GPUs sized for the 70B quantized variant and allow autoscale to add up to +20 GPUs for short bursts (use staged warming to avoid cold starts). Total burst capacity target: baseline + warm-pool + burst adders = ~36 GPUs (counts will vary by SKU).

3) Graded fallbacks: prefer model tiering over degrading latency. Policy: primary -> lightweight quantized variant -> size-limited responses (tokens cap) -> degraded p95 up to 600ms. We'll provide the policy DSL for your ops team.

4) Headroom and admission control: recommend a 30% headroom target and token-level admission control that denies heavy long-context requests when queue depth > 1200 or estimated completion will push p95 above SLO. 

5) Network guardrails (draft): avoid hairpin NAT by colocating monitoring proxies in the same subnet; use a dedicated egress NAT gateway with per-timestep rate limiting; use jumbo MTU only if your internal switch fabric supports 9000 bytes end-to-end. We'll attach a short net-policy draft.

Next steps: Jonas will send the GPU-to-RPS math and a short runbook; Kim can finalize the NAT/egress rules; if that looks good we'll lock counts for procurement. Is Stratus OK with the 30% headroom assumption?

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: runway_calcs_v2.xlsx (workbook with token->RPS conversions, cost curves, and suggested GPU counts)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, Morgan SRE <morgan.sre@stratus.ai>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment capacity ask: Stratus weekly runway targets and burst profile

Morgan / team — quick technical math and a shortlist of network items. I'm keeping the assumptions explicit so we can tune once you confirm average tokens per request and percent of long-context calls.

Assumptions (conservative): avg tokens/request = 120; tokens/sec -> RPS = tokens/sec / 120.
- Sustained 2,500 tokens/sec => ~21 RPS. With greedy batching and batching window ~20ms we estimate p95 generation compute per RPS: L2-13B quantized on A100-80GB =~ 2.0x RPS per GPU (so need ~11 GPUs; we recommend 10 for cost then rely on caching to hit 21RPS).
- Peak 20k tokens/sec => ~167 RPS. Burst plan: warm-pool of 6 mid-to-large GPUs handling ~30 RPS each when batched for the 70B quantized variant (~180 RPS). That aligns with our warm+burst suggestion in Vanessa's email.

GPU recommendation (SKU-agnostic counts): baseline: 10 GPUs (sustained L2-13B), warm-pool: 6 GPUs (70B quantized), burst headroom autoscale: +20 GPUs available via pre-approved capacity.

Network notes:
- NAT: use a single egress NAT gateway with SNAT pools to avoid ephemeral port exhaustion; enable connection tracking timeouts tuned for short-lived control-plane flows.
- MTU: enable jumbo frames only if NICs + TOR switches + aggregation support 9000; otherwise 1500 and tune TCP window sizes.
- Flow control: implement per-node egress policers to avoid a single GPU node saturating the 10Gb pipe during checkpointing or model download.

Attachment: net_policy-draft.md (detailed firewall/egress and NAT recommendations).

I'll open a small internal test ticket to simulate the 15-minute sustained 20k token burst in our staging harness — Karthik, can you schedule the run in 10 business days?

-Jonas
Senior Infra Eng, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: net_policy-draft.md (text file, recommended iptables/nftables snippets, NAT sizing guidance)

From: Morgan SRE <morgan.sre@stratus.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@stratus.ai
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment capacity ask: Stratus weekly runway targets and burst profile

Thanks, team — this is helpful. A couple clarifications before we lock procurement: 

1) Queueing / admission controls: what does "queue depth > 1200" map to in terms of user-visible retries? We run a 10s client timeout; we need to know whether admission denies will return 5xx vs 429 vs a partial response so we can adjust client retry logic.

2) Fallback behavior: we like the model-tiering idea. For the 30% of long-context 70B traffic, can Redwood provide an automated downgrade path so the client sees a structured response that indicates quality-tier used? We need that for auditability.

3) Pre-warming: how long to spin a 70B quantized instance from cold to warm? If a burst happens without sufficient warm pool, what's the expected additional p95 impact (rough ballpark)?

If you can answer these 3 items we can confirm the headroom and let procurement order the initial server & switch units.

-Morgan
Capacity Lead, StratusAI

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Morgan SRE <morgan.sre@stratus.ai>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, procurement@stratus.ai
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 17:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private deployment capacity ask: Stratus weekly runway targets and burst profile

Morgan — agreed on next steps and decision log below. Answering your questions inline and capturing owners.

1) Admission controls & client-visible errors: admission denies should return 429 with a structured JSON body describing "reason": "capacity" and "suggestedRetrySecs": 5. We prefer 429 so clients can retry with backoff; 5xx reserved for infra failures. Owner: Karthik Iyer.

2) Fallback & auditability: Redwood will tag responses with a header and response field ("x-redwood-model-tier": "primary|quantized|degraded") and include a compact provenance blob if the model was downgraded. That will satisfy your audit requirement. Owner: Jonas Weber (implement policy DSL) + Kim (log schema).

3) Pre-warm timings: rough numbers (lab measurements): 70B quantized cold->ready ~120-180s (model load dominated). Warm-pool instant warm start < 5s for cached KV/weights if using pinned RAM + persistent mmap-backed cache. Cold spin will add ~300-600ms to p95 per request during load; worst-case several seconds while internal warming completes — so warm pool is essential for your 5-15 minute burst profile. Owner: Karthik to validate in staging load test.

Decision log (approved):
- Lock initial counts for procurement: baseline 10 GPUs + warm-pool 6 + reserved autoscale slots 20 (procurement to order 36 GPUs equivalent capacity).
- Headroom target: 30% during sustained; allow p95 up to 600ms during peaks.
- Network guardrails: apply the net_policy-draft with dedicated egress NAT and per-node policers. Kim to finalise rules and share before vendor order.

Action items: 
- Karthik Iyer: schedule staging burst test (JIRA INF-4821) and validate cold vs warm p95 numbers (due 2026-12-10).
- Jonas Weber: deliver policy DSL and runbook for autoscale/fallback (due 2026-12-08).
- Kimberly Park: finalise net policy and porting checklist for your infra team (due 2026-12-06).
- Stratus procurement: confirm order window and lead times; we'll hold counts while purchase is initiated.

If that all looks good we'll update INF-4821 and route the procurement worksheet to Lisa. Thanks everyone for the quick turn.

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
